cohort: The study included 34 lower ureteral stenosis patients, with 14 undergoing Robot-assisted laparoscopic ureteral bladder reimplantation (RALUR) and 20 undergoing traditional laparoscopic ureteral reimplantation (LUR).
finding: Robot-assisted laparoscopic ureteral bladder reimplantation (RALUR) resulted in significantly shorter operation time, less postoperative hemoglobin decline, faster recovery, and shorter hospital stays compared to traditional laparoscopic ureteral reimplantation (LUR), though with higher total hospitalization costs.
